utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. They may be better over the top of your head, not behind. The earphones. Thank you. Please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The affirmation you made to tell the truth still applies. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mircic.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We will resume. The binder is before you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D001-6283.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 8. This is a criminal report dated 29 June 1998 submitted to the district public prosecutor's office in Pec against six individuals. If you look at page 3 in both languages, in the statement of reasons, because of which the report was filed, it is stated that on the 25th of June, 1998, around 4.30 they unloaded a shipment of weapons in the village of Jasic, Decani municipality in the presence of members of DTG. I merely wanted to ask you whether this reflects your information about the situation in the Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This report was submitted by the state security by their office in Djakovica which was under the Prizren centre. It is correct that on page 3 there is a description stating that in Jasici, in the school there, which is close to Decani and Junik next to the Albanian border, our operational information states that the information contained therein is correct, and that there was a shipment of weapons there which was to be distributed to the Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00911, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we next see D106.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 9. Mr. Mircic, this is a decision by Minister Stojiljkovic dated 19 July 1998. In paragraph 1, it is stated as follows: "For having distinguished themselves in carrying out the security tasks of prevention of terrorism in the area of the Autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija since 20 July 1998, I hereby award the PJP, SAJ, and JSO members with 50 dinars for every day of engagement." Have you had occasion to see this decision before?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I have. I saw it at the collegium meeting of the SUPs of chief in Djakovica. We were informed that pursuant to a specific article of the Law on the Interior, the minister made this decision that the following persons be awarded for having distinguished themselves in service.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next go to D107.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is the next tab, tab 10. I'll have a few questions about that. Here you can see a dispatch of the staff of the ministry dated 20 October 1998 where it says in para 1: "In accordance with the ministry's decision on rewarding PJP members, SAJ, and JSO members, for excelling in the implementation of security related tasks in the area of Kosovo and Metohija, lists must be drawn up from the period from 18 September to 17 October 1998 (at 50 dinars per day)." First of all, are you familiar with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was familiar with it because it was sent to all chiefs and general affairs departments in the SUPs in Kosovo and at the collegium session we were acquainted with the dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Does this dispatch have anything to do with the decision we just saw?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it comes as a result of the decision issued by the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us that within your OUP for your own purposes and records, you also kept records of PJP members being engaged in certain tasks, that is to say, when they left and came back after which they would again be assigned to regular duties. Is this dispatch in line with the register you kept?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D108 next.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 11. Another dispatch of the ministry staff in Pristina dated 3 August 1998. Without reading the whole thing, I just wanted to ask you to acquaint yourself briefly with the dispatch and comment. First I'd like to know whether you are familiar with it, and if so, please tell us something about it.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course I'm familiar with it. At a working meeting of the chiefs of secretariat we were acquainted with the dispatch of the MUP staffs signed by General Sreten Lukic. Given that the staff in Pristina was established by both public security and state security sectors, it is -- there's information here stating that certain Albanians who participated in the terrorist activities at KiM are making use of falsified doctored certificates and in order to escape mop-up terrorist operations and used to enter towns. Because of this, certain measures were proposed. One of which were detail searches of individuals and bringing them in for criminal investigation for identification checking operative and criminal records, conducting paraffin tests, as well as other operational and investigative measures in keeping with the Law on the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D109.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 12. Again the same question. This seems to be another dispatch of the MUP staff in Pristina dated 3 August 1998. Are you familiar with it? I won't read it out. It is rather brief. Please read it to yourself and provide a brief comment of the contents.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is another dispatch that was shown to us at the collegium of the secretariat chiefs. It was read out to all those in attendance and distributed forward. It also contains information of possible attacks by terrorist groups in some towns or municipal centres in order to take them. Based on that information, certain measures are proposed. Given that in keeping with the instructions for the defence of inhabited places, it is necessary to draw up defence plans for each municipal centre and submit them to the staff by 6 August 1998 at the latest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down when reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to this and in order to provide timely and accurate information, you also need to submit reports/dispatches --

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please read out slowly and approach the microphone.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to this and in order to provide timely and accurate information, you also need to submit reports/dispatches on incidents in which policemen were killed or wounded to the secretariats in which they worked. This resembles the other dispatch we saw when we discussed the PJP concerning reporting from the field on those killed and wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next see D240, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 13. Mr. Mircic, this is a dispatch of the ministry staff in Pristina dated 9 August 1998. I'm particularly interested in the last paragraph where it is stated that measures need to be taken in different companies which have construction machinery in order to demolish and fill in bunkers, shelters, trenches, and other features constructed by the terrorists for protection and firing on the police and members of the Yugoslav Army so that they cannot occupy and use them again. First of all, tell us, please, whether in the territory of your OUP there were such features, things like bunkers, trenches, and shelters, and if there were any, please tell us about their location?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in every village in my area there were bunkers, trenches, which were there for protection in case of attack of Serb forces. We can basically say that each and every village had such bunkers and trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Who dug out those trenches and who built those bunkers?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The villagers themselves. They were basically forced by the KLA so that there is some protection in case of an attack by the Serb police.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Who made use of those trenches and bunkers?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were used by KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D008-0550. It is your tab 14. We can move on to the next page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, this is a record of the hand-over of weapons in Junik on the 23rd of August, 1998. Are you familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with it. This is a record of weapons found in the village of Junik, Decani municipality, in a large bunker used as a depot. For some reasons, the KLA must have left those weapons there probably to distribute them further in different villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D00912, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see D006-4490.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: That's your tab 15. Mr. Mircic, this is a statement by Adrian Kumnova given to an authorised official of the Republic of Serbia MUP on the 24th of August 1998 in the Djakovica SUP premises. And in the first paragraph of this statement that person states that a member of the illegal terrorist group for Djakovica with headquarters in the village of Glodjani, Decani municipality, which is where the reception centre is located for members of sabotage terrorist group for the territory of Ras Dukagjini, I became a member of that group voluntarily in June of 1998. And then further on in the middle of that page, he says on the following day, When the flag was raised at 700 hours by Ramush Haradinaj of Glodjane village, who was a commander of the staff of DTG, which is a sabotage terrorist group from Metohija, we were told and then so on and so on. What I want to know is what did you know about the village of Glodjane and what did you know about Ramush Haradinaj?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our information concerning the village of Glodjane in Decani municipality was always derived from intelligence sources. We always had timely information and confirmed information that in this territory and in this village there was a staff or headquarters located of the members of a DTG sabotage terrorist group headed by Ramush Haradinaj who was a commander for the Metohija area. In this village, which is located quite close to Jablanica and strategically was a very favourable position for them for training and other activities and exercises, Ramush Haradinaj created and recruited a group there with members whom he trained in order to carry out sabotage and terrorist acts against the members of the Yugoslav police and army. You can see that based on the statement of a member of this group who stayed in the village of Glodjane. Intelligence information -- confirmed intelligence indicated that in Glodjane, there was also a prison which served to keep members of Serb ethnicity there who had been kidnapped in the territory of other villages in Decani municipality and brought there to be questioned. As I have said yesterday, due to some friendly relations, one such person was released and the rest were kept there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see page 2 of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And on the second page this person says, Exactly 14 days ago, together with a DTG from Djakovica at about 900 hours in the village of Prilep, fire was opened from ambush on the members of police. This was a terrorist act on our part. Does this correspond to the information you had about the activities of terrorists, and does this -- is this consistent with information you had about the location?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that in this period of time which this person mentions in the village of Prilep there was a terrorist attack against members of the MUP of Serbia. We had both fatalities among them and also seriously injured persons. Prilep was also quite favourable strategically for members of the KLA because it was located in the vicinity of Glodjane, and it gravitated towards other villages in the border area, border with Albania. That was a very important corridor for them, for infiltration of further terrorist groups and weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: When speaking of Prilep, can you please tell us its exact location, rather, did it have anything to do with the main road between Djakovica and Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Prilep was 5 kilometres from Decani, and there is a main road there between Decani and Djakovica. The main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mircic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00913, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see now D008-5356.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It's your tab 16. Mr. Mircic, this is a record on receipt of a criminal report which was filed with the Djakovica SUP but also with the Decani OUP. We see here that an injured party, Ljubisa Radunovic, submitted a criminal report about the fact that Milos Radunovic and Milica Radunovic were abducted. Are you familiar with this document, and were there such events in the territory of your OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this document. As I have said just a minute ago, in the village of Glodjane, Decani municipality, there was a KLA prison under the command of Ramush Haradinaj. And as I have said to you, there were Serbs that had been taken into custody and kept in that prison by them. So the possibility is that these persons were also kept in that prison in Glodjane. This criminal report was filed by the son of the Radunovic family.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00914, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D008-5359.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Your tab 17, Mr. Mircic. Again, this is a record on receipt of a criminal report filed with the Djakovica SUP but also forwarded to the Decani OUP. In this case, it involves an abduction by terrorist Albanians of Milan Vlahovic, but by --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: By Albanian terrorists, abduction of Veko and Milovan Vlahovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this situation?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know of this case and I know of this document, and as I've said earlier to you, all our intelligence on the fact that Serbs went missing in Decani municipality indicated that those who went missing were kept in this prison which was run by Ramush Haradinaj in the village of Glodjane.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell me, please, loyal citizens, those who were loyal to Serbia and to authorities, did they have problems with the KLA members?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we received numerous pieces of information from the ground that these people did encounter problems, these Albanians. That had to do with financial support of terrorists. These people had to dig trenches. They had to cook food, and play the role of logistic support for the members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the transcript, my question had to do with loyal citizens of Albanian ethnicity, that's what I was interested in, and it wasn't reflected in the transcript. Your Honours, I would like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D00915, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now see D242, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 18, if I'm not mistaken. Mr. Mircic, this is a dispatch by the staff number 3061 of 16 September 1998 concerning the missions and weaknesses in the work of the police. First of all, are you familiar with this document, and if so, would you please look at the first paragraph where these weaknesses are described.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this dispatch that came from the MUP staff in Pristina. It was signed by General Sreten Lukic. Again, this dispatch was read out to us at the collegium meeting of the SUP in Djakovica, and this dispatch stated that measures need to be taken against policemen who violate their duty in any way. They needed to act appropriately and have appropriate appearance as instructed by the rules of service within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P1202.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 19. Mr. Mircic, this is dispatch number 1685 dated 18 September 1998. It was signed on behalf of the assistant minister for the public security department, Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic. And my question to you is, are you familiar with this dispatch, and if so, could you briefly tell us what this dispatch is about, and does it have to do with regular routine, duties, and tasks within the area of work of the public security department?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this dispatch as well. It was read out at the collegium meeting of the Djakovica SUP. In the dispatch we can see what measures need to be taken and what intelligence was received from the field. We can see that important vital facilities need to be constantly toured and they need to be secured, both in operational terms and in intelligence terms. It needed to be done by police members, and it was all done within an action which had been implemented by the Ministry of the Interior by way of which explosives and mines were placed around the facilities which were of vital importance to the republic and to the province of Kosovo. This dispatch also instructed that the control of traffic in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija and transportation of any dangerous hazardous material needed to be stepped up.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Just to clarify what is stated in the transcript, did they mean that facilities needed to be protected against mines that could be placed and explosives that could be placed?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They -- what they meant is protection of these facilities against mines and explosive that could be placed by terrorists in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D429, please, which is your tab 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, this is a dispatch of the staff dated 14 September 1998 to the office of the minister. In paragraph 1 it is stated that on the 10th of September, 1998 in the village of Istinic, Decani municipality, members of the Ministry of the Interior held talks with representatives of the Siptar ethnic minority who had abandoned their homes during the armed operations carried out by Siptar terrorists. Anne Delforge, a representative of the International Red Cross from the Belgrade mission, was present during the talks. When the policemen called on the representatives of the Siptar ethnic minority from Istinic and other villages to return to their homes, Anne Delforge warned them on several occasions and asked the people present not to return to their homes because it was not safe, thus, causing panic, insecurity, and uncertainty among the residents on whether to return or not. Is any of this familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. Anne Delforge on several occasions during her visits in Decani municipality visited me in my office. We had an open and fair relationship. I also learned through my Albanian friends who are in Istinic that madam Anne Delforge was spreading propaganda among those who were present in Istinic to the effect that they should not go back to their homes because it wasn't safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, we see Istinic and a date of 10 September 1998. Can you tell us what was the situation like in Istinic village at the time? Are you familiar with it, and how?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am familiar with it. Based on our operational information and given than I hail from Decani and I spent my whole life with Albanians with whom I have friends, friendly relations, they trusted me greatly, in particular, when we discussed matters of their security. We had confirmed operational information that in Istinic village, Decani municipality, there were a lot of refugees from Decani and other villages and that there was a great concentration of civilians, women, children, the elderly there. Our assessment was that there were between 15- and 20.000 people there. The cause of that was fighting. Terrorists kept attacking police members in the general area of the municipalities of Djakovica and Decani in the village of Jablanica and so on and so forth. This was reason enough for these civilians to flee so as to avoid being caught in cross-fire during the clashes of the police and the KLA, and they feared for their safety. I tried to think of what we should do and how, given the great numbers of civilians, since General Djordjevic was in Kosovo and Metohija at that time touring our organisational units, trying to acquaint himself with the overall situation in the field as well as the work of the Ministry of the Interior and its members and whether they conducted themselves properly and in a fashion prescribed by the law, I made use of that opportunity to inform Mr. Djordjevic about the information we had concerning this great problem which we had in the village of Istinic and in Decani. I also proposed that we should try to tackle this issue peacefully and consistently in order to ensure the safety of those civilians. General Djordjevic agreed with my proposal, and I clarified for him further that I had friends among those people believing -- and I believed that we could negotiate a peaceful hand-over of weapons of those civilians who were armed and those members of the KLA who were manning the barricades around the village of Istinic. In that conversation with him, or rather, during that conversation, the Assembly president of Decani, Milivoj Djurkovic arrived. He also had information indicating that there was a great number of civilians including children there. We suggested to him to make use of our contact with certain persons in Istinic in order to prepare foodstuffs and other supplies for the civilians as they may need them. This also included medical supplies.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interruption, but I just wanted to clarify one thing. Was this the president of the municipality or of the Assembly of the Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The municipal president.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Continue, please.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our further assessment, I suggested to General Djordjevic to send a friendly contact from Istinic, Elis Bajlaj [phoen] to Decani. He was a person of some standing in the community. He was supposed to go there to talk to the representatives of the village and civilians who were in Istinic to see whether they would agree to a voluntary hand-over of weapons. Otherwise, should the clashes continue, given that there were many civilians there, it could all result in a great number of civilian casualties. General Djordjevic agreed to my proposal, and we followed it up. We received information after awhile by Elis Bajlaj that our proposal was well received on a voluntary hand-over of weapons by the KLA and others in the village of Istinic. This contact with Elis Bajlaj and Madjun Mucaj from the village of Gornja Lupa [phoen] was established by myself personally. I agreed with them on the exact time of our entry in Istinic. I enjoyed full confidence with these people and I trusted them in turn too because they were people whom one could trust and who were respected members of their community. As far as I recall, around 4.00 p.m., that was sometime in September, if I'm not mistaken, General Djordjevic and I together with the municipal president of Decani as well as with Zoran Andjelkovic who was president of the temporary Executive Council of Kosovo and who was there following a request made by the municipal president of Decani because of the growing complexity of the security situation in Istinic ... We set out from the OUP in Decani. I, General Djordjevic, the municipal president; and Zoran Andjelkovic, president of the temporary executive council of Kosovo and Metohija, in an official vehicle without any escort by any members of police units. Given that the village of Istinic is adjacent to Decani, the distance was perhaps as little as 3 kilometres to the very centre of Istinic. En route to Istinic, we saw tractors loaded with significant amounts of weapons, light infantry weapons as well as artillery pieces such as recoilless guns, machine-guns of 12.7 millimetres, mines and explosives on their way towards the OUP in Decani. They waved to us on their way there, they greeted us. Upon entering the village of Istinic, we realised that all barricades had been removed so as to enable us to enter. Along the road we could see a number of trenches and bunkers which had been used by KLA members. When we arrived at the centre of Istinic, certain representatives of the village, whom I mentioned and others, welcomed us warmly. They greeted us in a truly friendly manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting you. Did you enjoy any police escort at that moment?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment we had no police escort. We had no need for one given that there was mutual trust. We believed that we should not bring along any policemen so as not to irritate the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We have to rewind a bit to the beginning of the event. When General Djordjevic came to see you in Decani, according to your information, was he familiar with the situation in Istinic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. General Djordjevic had no information about Istinic. It was my official duty to inform him of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What ensued after your entry in the village?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we entered the village and spoke to the representatives of all villages, we agreed to enter an Albanian home where we sat down and discussed all the issues on the mind of those who had fled from the other villages. The municipal president and Zoran Andjelkovic promised to put in place certain measures in order to supply the population with food, medical supplies, and other necessities. We also established a point in the centre of Istinic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Witness's microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the last several sentences because the microphone was off for some reason.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So as it was agreed with representatives of other villages and the village of Istinic, in one Albanian house our relationship was friendly and a correct one, and nobody could have ever guessed that anything was happening in that area. And from the very expression on the faces of the refugees, you could see that they had hardly waited for the situation in the village of Istinic to be resolved. So as I said, we undertook certain measures to supply them with food, water, and other necessary supplies, medicines, and so on. This was organised by the municipal president and Zoran Andjelkovic as president of the temporary Executive Council of Kosovo and Metohija. Also we set a point in the centre of the village where weapons could be handed over. A large amount of weapons were handed over, heavy weapons and light weapons, explosive devices. Those were handed over by civilians coming from various villages within the municipality of Decani. The intelligence indicated that members of the KLA were also among the refugees, but they were wearing civilian clothes. I can also add that in the village of Istinic, in the very centre of the village, there was a mosque. I received information from my Albanian friends that in that mosque there were several persons who were wounded during the conflicts between terrorists and the police. So they asked me, and in fact, they led me to the mosque to show these injured persons to me. I entered the mosque, I saw about a dozen persons there, they were all exhausted, wounded. And we immediately undertook certain measures. We invited an ambulance from the territory of the municipality of Pec, and we also invited physicians of both Albanian and Serbian ethnicity who came to the centre of Istinic. They took over the wounded and took care of them in the hospital in Pec. So this is an example of how we operated in the field and how we took care of the civilian population and assisted them in any way possible at any moment. If you can just imagine given the quantity of weapons there and the concentration of weapons was really inconceivable. If there was a provocation by terrorists or indeed an armed conflict, very very many civilians would have ended up as casualties.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mircic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now move on. I would kindly ask the Exhibit D244.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 21. Mr. Mircic, this is a dispatch of the MUP staff number 1026 dated 20th September, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following page in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with this dispatch? And if you are, could you please focus on item 1?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm familiar with this dispatch, I will not repeat how I learned about it so here it was requested for a list of villages to be compiled, those villages who handed over weapons, ammunition, mines and explosives, and other military equipment with information on the amounts broken down by type for each village separately and together. So this was a dispatch of the staff signed by General Sreten Lukic who requested us to collect all the information concerning the weapons that were handed over, and that information had to be submitted to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mircic. Under item 4, we can see a list of villages where refugees have returned and the number of returnees. When we are talking about this item, if we could briefly go back to the situation in Istinic, could you please tell us whether the people who were in Istinic on that day, did they go back to their villages either on that day or on any of the following days?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I forgot to say that. On the same day when we were there, they could hardly wait to go back, and this was also our wish to help them go back. Many of them had transportation of their own, some of them didn't. They used their tractors and wagons, but for that purpose Zoran Andjelkovic and president of the municipality provided a bus. And it was not a bus of the ministry, but it was a regular bus which was used to transport the population to their villages. We told them that it was safe and that they could go back and continue living in their own villages. And this was indeed done, so all the persons who were in Istinic and who came from the villages in the territory of this municipality of Decani and other area, they went back to their respective villages without any pressure from the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mircic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see the Exhibit D431.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 22, sir. Mr. Mircic, these are the minutes from Djakovica SUP OUP Decani, dated 29th of September that had to do with the weapons and ammunition handed over or discovered by members of MUP or handed over by the Albanian population in the municipality of Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I'm not mistaken, Your Honour, this document, at least according to the translation that we did have before, was translated in such a way that the numbers that are there in the Serbian version were not all listed in the English translation, but we could only see the final numbers, the totals, in English. Is so if we could please have a look at the Serbian version, this is page 5 in Serbian. And I believe it is on the following page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Mircic. Here we can see automatic guns of Chinese production finishing with the number 725.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, this is correct. So these weapons mostly came from the village of Istinic. And they were handed over voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Just a minute, Mr. Popovic. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I may be mistaken, Your Honour, but in the English version I have I don't have the complete document in the page that's being displayed in the B/C/S. It at least was not included in my copy of the English. I don't know if other pages are also missing in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you know about this, Mr. Popovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I know, Your Honour, and this is what we already discussed before you. When this document was translated, they did not mention all the numbers of weapons that you can see in the Serbian version, but in the translation, they only mentioned the totals of weapons, the same totals that are mentioned in the Serbian version, and this translation was in this form admitted into evidence because all the totals correspond fully to the totals in the original. It is just that these 725 automatic rifles are not listed fully in the English translation, so not all of their numbers are listed in the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 7, if I'm not mistaken. Yes, it is page 7 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, these are semi-automatic rifles of Chinese production. The total number is 419.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. These are all the numbers from the rifles and you can see the total.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to page 9 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Here we can see the machine-gun and also machine-gun of calibre 7.62, 54 pieces. Also machine-gun Browning, 35 pieces. So does this correspond to your recollection of what you saw in Istinic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a well famous fact that the terrorist use these types of weapons in their actions and they brought these weapons from the territory of Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please take a look at the last page, this is page 11. I believe this is on the following page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Here we can see hand-held rocket-launchers and you can see the numbers here, also mortars, seven pieces. Is this the kind of weapons that people in Istinic and elsewhere in the territory of OUP Decani had?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they even had Ambrust anti-rocket system for air defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, the weapons discovered in the village of Istinic, could it be seen by foreign observers?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all of these weapons that was turned over voluntarily by the Albanian national minority was displayed in the facility of the OUP Decani, and we allowed access to anybody who wanted to see the kinds of weapons that the terrorists in the territory of the municipality of Decani had. And we also did have visitors who were, in fact, representatives of diplomatic world and media and who also represented this in the various media.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell me whether in the territory of the OUP Decani, you had members of the reserve police departments?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know anything concerning the local security?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the local security was established in my territory approximately, there were about ten such security units in villages of Istinic, Gornje Jaouka [phoen] and so on. And they signed work contracts with presidents of municipality, and they voluntarily agreed that they would receive uniforms, ID cards, and light weapons. And in those work contracts, it was clearly stipulated what were their authorities and their duties in the villages in which they performed those duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But first of all, what was the nationality of the members of the local security?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously they were of the Albanian nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us who organised members of the local security? Yes, who organised them, let's start from that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I spoke to my friends, my acquaintances, and we agreed that it was a good idea to set up such local security. I explained why. I explained that they could communicate better with the population there. They could see what were the supplies there or that were needed, and they could be mindful that the members of the KLA did not enter the village and cause any conflicts with our members, which would obviously jeopardise the local population. And then they arranged it with local authorities in the municipality of Decani, and the municipality was obliged to provide them with all the necessary equipment. The equipment was indeed provided and handed over to them so that they could use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that we are talking about this, I will kindly ask the Exhibit D005-0011.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 23. Mr. Mircic, here you can see one such work contract the contract signed by Mihil Abazi from the village of Oseh Hilja, municipality of Djakovica, if I'm not mistaken. Could you please tell me if such work contracts or contracts of employment were signed with members of the local security?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the same format of contract was also used in the municipality of Decani, so we used the same form, and the procedure was the same in all the municipalities in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, the same one in Decani and elsewhere, and you can see here that this is the contract of employment, and you can see all the authorities given to members of the local security.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So Article 1 stipulates their duties and obligations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And they were in daily contact with us, in daily co-operation. They also conveyed new information that they had. They took care about the security of their population.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did they have uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They had uniforms and official IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Were they armed?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They had light weapons, pistols.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Who provided these arms to them?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The arms were handed out by the president of the municipality, the same one who signed such contracts of employment.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether members of the local security were attacked by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period we had one attack on the family of Madjun Mucaj in the village of Gornje Luka. He was a member of the local security for the village of Gornje Luka. During the night, terrorist groups sneaked into the village and carried out an attack by way of firing from automatic weapons onto the house and onto the gate leading into the yard of Madjun Mucaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, looking at this contract of employment in Article 3 it says here that the co-ordinator of local security would have an ID. Did such IDs exist?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Before we move to the next document, I would like to tender this one into evidence, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00916, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see D008-4785.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 24. Mr. Mircic, here we can see a copy of an ID which reads "local security". Are you familiar with this, and is this what these IDs looked in the territory of Decani OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One can clearly see that such IDs were used by members of the local security, and the text was in both Albanian and Serbian, not just in one language.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00917, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D005-0015, which is tab 25 in your binder, Mr. Mircic. Could we see that document now, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the same one.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, here we can see an ID of local security, but we have the second page here as well. And on the second page it says that the bearer of the ID is authorised to work to secure infrastructure.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The authorities that he has, the powers that he has.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That he can bear weapons?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are the authorities, or rather, the powers that members of local security had.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, could this be admitted into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00918, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now D005-0001.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 26. Mr. Mircic, this is a list of local police, Djakovica municipality, listing the first and last names of persons, the village that they were from, their citizen registration number, and the weapons that was issued to them with the number. Are you familiar with such lists, and did they exist in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they certainly existed. These are the records kept by Decani municipality just like all other municipalities in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And these lists that you saw for Decani municipality, did they have the same information about weapon, uniform, and the village that the person was from?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. All of the information for persons who were on the local security was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, could I tender this into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be Exhibit D00919, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have concluded with a topic, and I would move to another one but seeing that it's time for the break, perhaps it would be better to have our first break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, we'll have the first break. We will resume at 11.00. A Court Officer will assist you during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we now see D007-0208.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: That is your tab 27. Mr. Mircic, this is a criminal report dated 28 September 1998. It was filed by the secretariat in Djakovica because the injured persons who are listed in this criminal report were the victims in this event whose perpetrators are not known. The criminal report on page 3 states that their bodies were found after they were beaten and tortured in a location where the Locanska Bistrica canal links up with Radonjicko lake. That this is where their bodies were found. So my question so to you is, do you you know about this event described in this criminal report, and if so, can you tell us what is this about? So for the sake of the transcript, I said the Radonjicko lake.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about this criminal report, and I know about the event in that area near Radonjicko lake and the canal which passes through the entire territory of Decani municipality, which empties the river into Radonjicko lake, and it is located in the territory between Djakovica and Decani. We spoke earlier about the village of Glodjane where there was a prison where Serbs were held and that that prison was run by Ramush Haradinaj. Their bodies were found there in that canal at the place where the canal flows into the lake. This is where the bodies of the victims were found, the victims were of Serb ethnicity, and they had been tortured and killed, shot dead by KLA members. Their bodily remains were found there.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, upon examining of this criminal report, we can see that there are some Albanians mentioned there too, the first five are Serbs, but then several names afterwards, Hota Isufi and so on are Albanians. Are they indeed Albanians?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Albanians but of Catholic faith. They were persons from Djakovica municipality who were members of some local security. There were Roma there as well, persons of Roma ethnicity who were taken to that prison and tortured and eventually killed by the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By your leave, I also have some information about witnesses who have survived, people who had been taken to be shot by the KLA and survived, shot by Ramush Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Continue.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we received information after the departure of the -- of KFOR that some Albanians had been shot by the KLA, and those were the Albanians who had been in contact with the state security service and public security service who were loyal citizens. Sinan Musaj [phoen] and Muriqi [phoen] who escaped from the execution site, we received information from him that was in Dasinovci village near Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we have this admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This would be Exhibit D00920, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. D008-0584, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: This is your tab 28. Mr. Mircic, this is the analysis of the work of Djakovica SUP OUP Decani for the period August to September 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we see page 3 in both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: The heading is "Crime" and then in paragraph 2 it says that all crimes that were committed in August were committed by unidentified perpetrators under Article 125, entitled "Terrorism." And that a result of those events a number of policemen were killed. Then they go on to say that on the 2nd of August, 1998, a terrorist attack was carried out against MUP members in the village of Prilep and that two MUP members were killed and a number of them sustained serious or slight injuries. Then on the 9th of August, 1998, an attack was carried out against MUP members in the village of Prilep as a result of which four members of MUP were killed and a number of them injured gravely or slightly. So, Mr. Mircic, we saw that in two attacks in the village of Prilep six MUP members were killed in August only, August of 1998. So what can you tell us about the events in the village of Prilep in that period of time?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned earlier that there were attacks in the area of the village of Prilep, and I can confirm that there was a very important KLA stronghold there and that on that road, the main road between Decani and Djakovica, terrorists repeatedly attacked policemen, police check-points and so on especially in the village of Prilep, as I have mentioned earlier. That area was of great strategic importance for the KLA members because that area enabled them to bring in weapons from Albania and take them to the mountain area and to the village of Junik. This is why they worked so hard on maintaining that corridor. And that village always had very strong presence of their forces because it was in the vicinity of Glodjane. This is why there was serious combat there on many occasions in which there were many victims on the MUP side, among MUP members. They used heavy mortars, hand-held rocket-launchers, heavy machine-guns, recoilless guns. Terrorists also used explosive devices, they mined certain facilities, bridges on the river which passes through Prilep. The river is called Locanska Bistrica, so their stronghold in Prilep was linked to Rznic and Rastavica villages. This is why they had a very strong presence of their forces there. As I said, they had great interests in the area. In these operations a number of facilities were damaged, that is to say houses in the village of Prilep. It's a large village, over 150 houses, so the area where combat took place was right next to the main road, Decani Djakovica, perhaps 10 metres on either side of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say that there were many damaged houses, where were they located?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said already, close to the main road, 5 to 10 metres on either side of it. You know what Albanian villages look like, it's one house to the next with tall -- with high walls around the plots, concrete walls, so sometimes they resemble bunkers.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the situation was like with the other houses in the village, which were not close to the road?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Such houses did not sustain any damage. As I said, Prilep is a rather large village adjacent to Rznic and towards Rastavica so it's not a village of 10 or 15 houses but of 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In that period when the combat casualties occurred, were there any civilians in Prilep?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there were no civilians left. They had left the village further in the territory of Decani municipality. One of those was also Istinic which we mentioned. There were no civilian casualties in this village for that reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to the next page in both languages. There is a subtitle there: Structure of Violations of Public Order and Law. We see that in September there was one violation. Can you offer a brief comment of what we can see?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are standard items in such reports when reporting on the situation in the field. We can see here that no Albanian reported any crimes in this period. The brawl mentioned or the fight mentioned occurred among the Serbs who were in Decani, so it was not caused by any ethnic reasons. In Decani itself, there were many Albanians, but they did not leave or flee. They enjoyed protection and left their houses in a usual fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]Let's go to the next page in the Serbian, and let us stay on this page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It has to do with weapons and ammunition. We have discussed this in detail when we have reviewed the lists. Is this what we were discussing about the village of Istinic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, this is different information about smaller quantities of weapons handed over by the villagers from other villages in Decani.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we see any mention made of 942 rifles?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I think it says something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Go to the next page in the Serbian. This is what I'm asking you about.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see. This is all from Istinic. This is part of the regular report for that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's go to the last paragraph, Disciplinary Liability. We see that there was one report for breach of discipline in September. What was it about?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this was an officer from the OUP, assistant commander Mr. Jukic who committed a grave breach of discipline as well as the crime of theft. We found in his possession a number of vehicles and tractors in his courtyard. He was suspended from work, and a criminal report was filed against him as well as disciplinary procedure initiated against him. He was suspended from work immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you treat all those of whom you learned had committed a crime in this same fashion? Please wait before answering so that the interpreters could catch up.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. We always followed up in such cases when the conduct of MUP members was concerned. Whenever we learned that they had committed a crime or a misdemeanour, adequate measures were taken in keeping with the Law on the Interior. I just wanted to add something while we are discussing the issue of disciplinary liability. In 1998 we took measures in a case involving four persons who were murdered. Sloba Jovanovic, a Serb from Decani municipality, from Decani itself, committed the murder of four persons, that is to say, of two families who were in an apartment building in Decani. These were elderly people. I know that one family name was Barjaktari, and I can't recall the other last name. I don't want to speculate. He did this in an illegal way. We received certain information. We carried out a full on-site investigation and other investigative measures ascertaining that this was a very serious crime. Through operational work and by application of other measures, we discovered the perpetrator. We brought him in and handed him over to the competent investigating judge of the district prison in Pec. Detention was pronounced and in further proceedings he was sentenced to 15 years of imprisonment. In 1999 the proceedings were conducted in Leskovac outside Kosovo. The whole case was heard there, and he received 15 years in prison. Our state and our service never tried to cover up such instances or to show them as being something completely different to what they actually were.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00921, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, did you know that in October 1998 there was an agreement signed between Mr. Holbrooke and Milosevic by which verifiers were to be introduced into the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that. As I said, I was aware of that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contact with the verifiers?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I recall, we received instructions by way of a dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We'll see that. But before that, I wanted you to tell me something about the following: What kind of relationship did you have with the verifiers, and what was the relationship like between the verifiers and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had a fair and good co-operation with all verifiers who came to see me. They were welcome, and we always had good discussions. I believe our co-operation in the field was quite good. As for the relationship of members of the monitoring mission and the KLA, we had information which indicated that the verifiers were biased in favour of the KLA terrorist groups. Operational information confirmed our belief because it was confirmed that they provided the KLA with information about our forces and positions, et cetera. In a way, they provided logistical support to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see P1041.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your number 29. This is a dispatch of the ministry staff in Pristina. Under A we see this: "In accordance with item 1/8 of the agreement the mission has the status of a diplomatic body. In connection with this, mission members should be treated in the manner prescribed." Are you familiar with this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am. This was an instructional dispatch on how to treat OSCE mission members advising us of their diplomatic status and the necessity to treat them fairly and provide them with the conditions necessary for their work. We followed this through.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the next page under B. We have reporting and informing.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this mentions urgent and daily reports submitted according to previously ordered measures. This has to do with the dispatches we saw which preceded this one with the information about what those measures were. We had daily information on the KLA. There were provocations and fire being opened at MUP members. Each terrorist attack was referred to as well as the location and time. This was kept in the duty officer's log-book in the SUP of Djakovica. And in Djakovica, they compiled and collated all information received from the field sending it on to the staff and minister. This was the line of reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next see Exhibit D008-0478.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Just for the sake of transcript, can you tell me how did this line operate that you talked about, as it's slightly different in the transcript than you told us.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will tell you. All police members who were at certain locations on the ground and who were attacked by the KLA, whether these were provocations or attacks, would report the duty service of the OUP Decani about the area where that happened. The head of shift of the duty service of the Decani OUP was obliged to submit all the information to the head of the shift of the OUP Djakovica, and the head of shift of the Djakovica SUP would directly inform the staff and the staff would inform the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we can see the Exhibit D008-0478. It is your tab 30. It's a dispatch from the Djakovica SUP sent to the staff. Could we please see the next page in the version --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic, you've given two different numbers at lines 2 and 14. 0478 or 7408, which would you like?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, the first one I said, D008-0478, and that is the document which we can see on the screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, under your tab 30 you can see in item 2 that it's a dispatch of the 27th of March, 1999, sent to the MUP staff in Pristina. Item 2 mentions terrorist acts for the 27th of March in Ljumbarda village, Decani municipality, in the period of 11.00 and then 1545 hours. So this is already a moment when the NATO bombing campaign over the territory of Serbia had started. Can you tell us if this reflects the security situation on the ground in that period?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was a regular report in the case of NATO aggression which started on the 24th of March, and in accordance with the instruction dispatch, we reported about events, the damage inflicted, about those who were injured, and all the other information that was of security interest, including terrorist attacks, provocations, everything that was interesting from the point of view of the security service. That included damaged facilities and persons who had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00922, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see D143.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 31. Mr. Mircic, this is a dispatch from the staff of the ministry in Pristina dated the 1st of April, 1999. And my question for you is, first of all, whether you are familiar with this document?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just like with the other documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see that it says here: "In light of the new situation caused by the NATO bombardment and in order to keep the Ministry of the Interior effectively and timely informed, it is necessary that you submit ..." and then under certain items some things are enumerated. Can you please give us a short comment on what is enumerated here.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was like the usual information. This would be sent to the secretariat and all the measures mentioned in these items would be registered, would be then sent to everyone. It was the duty service of the SUP Djakovica, then they would send it to the staff, and the staff would send it to the minister. That was the usual reporting line.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, but please focus on page 2 of this document now, so could we please see page 2 in both versions. And under item 4 it says, Albanians and persons of other nationalities who have fled the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija, and certain things are ordered there. Before you tell me anything about that, my first question for you is, were you born in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was, as I said at the beginning. In Decani municipality, I spent my whole life there and my whole career in the Decani municipality with Albanians. I had many friends, colleagues, people with whom I engaged in sports, socialised, and so on and so forth. Maybe I forgot to say that I also worked in the municipal court in Decani for ten years. That was before I began working for the -- for the Serbian MUP. I had many friends among ethnic Albanians. I visited their homes, I attended their wedding and mournings and whatever the occasion was, I was always there together with them in restaurants in the streets, we always had contact, we always worked well together, and no one ever paid any attention to whether you were an ethnic Albanian or an ethnic Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell me as for the period that we are discussing now, that is the year 1999, did ethnic Albanians but also Serbs and Montenegrins leave the territory of Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a well known fact that both the Serbs and Montenegrins and ethnic Albanians would leave the territory of Decani and the municipality of Decani because they feared for themselves, they were worried about the fate of their families. Serbs mostly left in the direction of Serbia or Montenegro, whereas Albanians would also leave in the directions of Montenegro, Macedonia, or Albania. They were afraid for their lives, and they were afraid for their families because the war operations were going on between the KLA and the MUP, and they did not want to find themselves between these forces and under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, did you see refugees from other areas in Kosovo and Metohija who were possibly passing through the territory of Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We can say that from Pec through Istok and Klina these areas are connected by a road leading to Djakovica, and I was in a position to see long convoys of people, Albanians. I talked about them, what were the reasons why they were leaving, what was the problem. I tried to persuade them to stay in a nice and cultured manner, but they would always tell me, well, now, the NATO bombing is underway, there are also terrorist KLA groups who are in conflict with the police and army members and we do not feel safe. That was their response, so we could not violently stop anyone or prevent anyone from exercising their rights to do what they wanted to do at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, can you speak Albanian?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can speak it, I can write, I can read, I can translate.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: So when you talk to these ethnic Albanian refugees, what did they tell you? What were the reasons for which they were leaving the territory?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They even mentioned as reasons that the KLA was exercising pressure against them in order to create convoys and to produce some kind of humanitarian catastrophe, humanitarian disaster. They were also distributing leaflets, and they tried to spread panic among the population by using misinformation. They claimed that the Serbian forces were carrying out aggression against civilians in order to place that in the international media.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, do you know what was the per cent of Serbs and Montenegrins who left Decani during March, April, and May of 1999?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that as the number of Serbs and Montenegrins at the time, as I said earlier, was around 700 individuals, including women, children, the elderly, and the younger people, I can tell you that the entire population left the area except for the able-bodied men who were engaged with the army or with the MUP. Of course the monks also stayed there, they did not leave the Visoki Deci monastery.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, do you know how many Serbs are living in Decani today?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a single Serb living in Decani today except for the monks, let me repeat that once again. These are the brethren of the monastery Visoki Deci. There are about 30 of them. They welcome visitors and receive them and for the time being they are being protected by KFOR. These are the Italian units of KFOR.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, did you have any information that some inhumane measures were used in your territory?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, depleted uranium was used during the NATO bombing campaign. These were bombs that created huge craters and were very destructive. They contained depleted uranium.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see Exhibit D698.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: It is your tab 32.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, this is a document that represents the contents of a leaflet. Are you aware that leaflets of this kind were to be found in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, and if so, could you tell us anything about that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I am aware of that. Leaflets of this kind were thrown around in all areas of Kosovo and Metohija including the Decani municipality among the Albanian population. The KLA was doing that. The terrorist groups of the KLA or UCK in Albanian. I see here before me this pamphlet which I have seen earlier. We can even read it in Albanian or I can translate it. It calls on -- we call on you to evacuate temporarily from the territory of the Republic of Kosovo as they are already calling it at the time, which is dangerous at the moment. And the reason are the occupying Serbian forces. It then goes on to say that their army, the KLA that is to say, is not able to protect them because it does not have sufficient forces. Therefore, they instruct them to begin moving in the direction of Albania and Macedonia en masse. There were even people who were assigned to spread this kind of propaganda among the people. The KLA would send them out and the leaflet says we have NATO support and we shall win eventually. So that they would not be responsible in front of their people, they are telling them to keep moving out of the territory of Kosovo and Metohija so that they would protect their own lives, their own people, that is to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please see the document D008-0554.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Which is your tab 33. This is a dispatch from the Djakovica SUP sent to the MUP staff in Pristina on the 29th of May, 1999. Under item 2, a terrorist attack carried out on the 28th of May, 1999, is recorded in Ljumbarda village, Decani municipality. Certain members of the police were attacked and wounded. Does that correspond with your knowledge of about the security situation in the territory of the OUP in that period?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that happened on a daily basis, there's nothing new here. This was a regular incident that never stopped, and we can see that it was a DD dispatch, which means that it was a report that was urgent, and this was the usual procedure, as I said earlier when I talked about reporting.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I tender this document in to evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D00923, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, do you know General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What kind of a chief would I be if I did not know General Djordjevic, who was my immediate superior? I know him officially, not as a private person.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the last time you saw General Djordjevic in the area of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this period, I mean 1998, that was when we really did a big operation in the area of Istinic village. That was really exemplary, an exemplary operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see General Djordjevic in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija in the year 1999?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I never saw him in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija again.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mircic, did you ever in 1998 or 1999 see or hear that there was any kind of plan or agreement within the Ministry of the Interior by which the Albanian population in Kosovo and Metohija would be expelled from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw any such plan, nor did I ever hear about that, nor do I believe that anything like that existed. That was never the goal of the security forces to do something like that with the members of the ethnic minority, Albanian ethnic minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
