utterances.text: Did you ever during 1998 or 1999 see or hear that there was any kind of plan or agreement within the Ministry of the Interior by which the Albanian population would be expelled from Kosovo and therefore the ethnic composition of the Albanian population in Kosovo would be changed?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This was the last question in my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Popovic. Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Mircic.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, respected madam prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I want to go back to your evidence from yesterday. Yesterday and also today you've spoken about your role as a chief of the Decani OUP and you told us that you held that position both in 1998 and 1999 and that your direct superior was the SUP chief from Djakovica; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you've indicated that the SUP chief was called Kovacevic?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Do you recall his full name, Mr. Kovacevic's full name? Only if you remember.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps I'll be able to recall it later but not at this moment. I just remember his last name, Kovacevic. It's been quite awhile and perhaps I forgot.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's fine. It doesn't matter. Was Mr. Kovacevic chief of the Djakovica SUP both in 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I recall, he was appointed in mid-1998 and, yes, he was in the same position throughout 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You told us yesterday also that your OUP had about 80 P status personnel. I take it that by 80 P status personnel, you mean professional status personnel?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that is under the staffing scheme of the MUP of Serbia. We had 11 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: 111.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As per scheme, there should have been 180, but there were also OSL personnel, meaning authorised official. So P personnel were uniformed policemen carrying out their regular tasks in keeping with the Law on the Interior and the rules of service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if I understood your evidence correctly, in 1999 you had about 80 of them? 80 P status personnel in your OUP in Decani?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. In -- with two substations in Junik and Rznic. These were two substations which formed part of the Decani unit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Just to correct the transcript, you mentioned there were two substation, one in Junik and the other one is in which locality, could you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Rznic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also said yesterday that you had some reservist in your OUP, and you said given the number of population in the municipality of Decani, you had very few of them but there was some reservists in your OUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, when you say given the number of population in the municipality of Decani, do you mean given the number of Serb population in the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had in mind the overall population.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So did the number of reservists that were incorporated in police stations like yours depend on the number or the size of the population in a certain municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Since the army had its reservists.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And these reservists that were incorporated in your OUP, did they have some sort of police or military training that they had undergone before being incorporated in your OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For one to be a member of the reserve force, one must have had served their military term. That's one of the preconditions. No training, however, was undertaken when engaged in certain conditions. They only performed their regular duties of the police alongside active-duty members. Reservists never acted independently. They were there merely as a reinforcement to bring up staffing levels given that we had too few members of the regular force.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So if I understand your evidence correctly, reservists carried out the same functions as regular policemen only that they did not act independently, they were always accompanied by a regular police officer in carrying out their duties?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Were they issued the same type of uniforms and weapons and equipment that regular police officers had?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And would these -- you've said that they were brought in to the police force to reinforce or bring up staffing levels. I take it that this is something that did not only happen in your OUP but also in other police stations in other municipalities? This wasn't something specific to your OUP that you had reservists in your police force; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. This was not something specific to us alone. The same thing applied across all the organisational units of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You said that these persons would have been persons that had received some sort of military training previously. Would they generally be a bit older in age than regular police officers or active-duty police officers from your OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We always tried to have younger reservists. We also wanted to pick them out of a number of those who had served their military sentence so that they had undergone some sort of military training or military police training.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And so these would be persons who were picked out from the local community? They would be original to the Decani municipality, these reservists who would be called up to reinforce your police force?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't only Serbs who were reservists, there were also Albanians, members of the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, my question was whether they would be from the municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Solely from the municipality because the regulations said that you couldn't engage persons from other municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've also mentioned during the course of your evidence several times that you were a member of the collegium of the SUP in Djakovica; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand your question, a member of the collegium you said?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Let me rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you mean -- did you mean that I was a member of the collegium? Whether I was one?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, during the course of your examination by my colleague you were shown a series of documents sent by different officials from the MUP, and you indicated several times that you were shown these documents or you became acquainted with these documents during meetings of the collegium of the Djakovica SUP, so what I was asking was just for you to confirm whether that was the case, that you were a member of the collegium of the Djakovica SUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will explain this for you so that you become more familiar with this issue. Djakovica SUP had Decani OUP as an organisational unit. And I, as chief of the OUP by virtue of my position, belonged to the collegium of the Djakovica SUP. So whenever the chief of the secretariat found it necessary to convene a collegium meeting, then it would be convened, and we would come to that meeting where he informed us of any documents that had arrived, any regular reports on the work of the police. He would inform us of the security situation in our territory and so on. So those were the collegium meetings. I wasn't the only one who would attend, but chiefs of various organisational units would come, and it was part of their job description.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So if I understand correctly, these collegium meetings were attending not only by you but also by the Djakovica SUP chief and the heads of various organisational units that were within the territory of the Djakovica SUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And during the course of these meetings you've told us the SUP chief would inform you of any reports or dispatches that would arrive, and I suppose that concerned your scope of work?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That concerned my work and the work of the entire secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: During these meetings, would you also update the SUP chief about events in the area of your OUP? Would you also update him on what was going on in the Decani municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said earlier, the information was passed via duty service, so the duty service of the Decani OUP would inform the head of the shift in the Djakovica SUP on any events and the head of the SUP shift would inform in turn everybody else, chief of the SUP, heads of police departments about anything that may have happened in the territory. So it wasn't me who directly informed somebody. No, it was persons who were heads of shifts whose job description it was to pass the information on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. That's much clearer. And with what frequency were these collegium meetings held?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meetings were held whenever the chief found it necessary. The typical procedure was to have the collegium meetings every day and on some days the meetings could not be held due to the security situation, and there were also occasions when I couldn't attend collegium meetings due to terrorist activity that the terrorist groups conducted on the main road between Djakovica and the other town. They attacked all civilians, all traffic passing on the road. They had issued an order to their population not to use that road, not to move on that road, so Albanians never used that road. Whenever they saw somebody on that road, they knew that that person was a Serb or of other non-Albanian ethnicity, and such persons were typically injured or killed when using that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And on those occasions when you did not attend these daily collegium minutes [sic], how would you become acquainted or familiarise yourself with the issues that had been discussed there?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would receive a dispatch, and the chief of the secretariat would convey that to me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So if a dispatch was discussed at these collegium meeting and you had not attended, you would receive a copy of that, am I understanding correctly, from the SUP chief?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If communication lines were operational, then I would receive a dispatch, yes. And if not, they would just call me on the phone and brief me on the phone. Sometimes we communicated via courier service.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. You were shown several dispatches that you mentioned were discussed at these collegium meetings, and I want to go through two of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The first one is D107, if we could have that up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So this is a dispatch that's dated 20th of October, 1998, and we see it's sent by Major-General Sreten Lukic, and it's addressed to all SUP chiefs, and also to PJP units, SAJ, JSO, squad commanders, and if I recall your testimony correctly today you said that you had been informed about the contents of this dispatch at a collegium meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So although this is addressed to SUP chiefs, one of the instructions is that you had to compile list of informations of members who are not currently in unit for justified reasons but are entitled to some reward and it refers to rewarding PJP members, SAJ and JSO members. So my question is, once the SUP chief of Djakovica would communicate to you these instructions by General Lukic, then you would implement them, if I understand correctly? You would implement or carry out the instructions that are carried out here -- indicated here?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me clarify tis dispatch for you. You see that this dispatch says that it is sent to the chief and also to commanders of detachments who were not members of SUP collegium. And here in this dispatch, they are issuing tasks, commanders of detachments and PJP units were to act in accordance with this dispatch. I was merely briefed on this dispatch. It doesn't fall within my regular scope of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You did indicate earlier today that you also kept records of PJP members engaged in certain tasks, and you were asked, is this dispatch in line with the register you kept, and you said, yes, of course it is?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But when it comes to this dispatch, it is the police department in Djakovica, commander of the platoon, commander of the company, and the commander of the platoon within the Decani OUP who were the real addressees of this dispatch. They were the ones who were supposed to keep records and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we can see another one of these dispatches. This is 1202. P1202.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is another one of the dispatches that you were shown earlier, and this one is dated 18 September 1998. And we see the addressees on -- at the top, all SUP chiefs, the head of the MUP staff, border police stations, et cetera. There's a series of other organisational units indicated there, and in the second page which we don't need to turn to right this minute says that this is signed and sent by General Djordjevic. Do you recall looking at this dispatch earlier?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Let me look at it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And you indicated earlier today that this was -- you were familiar with this dispatch because it was also read out at the collegium meeting of the Djakovica SUP; do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in this dispatch, General Djordjevic is instructing the addressees to take a series of measures it says, and I'm reading somewhere in this second paragraph it says, Apart from intensifying the measures ordered in dispatch number 1150 of the 24th of September, 1997, it is necessary do the following. And there are a series of measures that are indicated there. You see that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see only the first page.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is in the first --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, these are standard measures undertaken by MUP when assessing the newly created situation in any area. These are normal measures that all organisational units within a secretariat should undertake. Once we have information that there could be situations where terrorist groups could endanger vital facilities, personal safety, endanger property, and it says here facilities of vital importance, then it's normal that the MUP should undertake certain measures of operational and intelligence measure -- nature.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And we see on page 1 that it refers to action plan of the Sat or watch action. If we could turn to the second page of the dispatch we see this is the paragraph, almost last paragraph, we see General Djordjevic instructing "start implementing the measures ordered having previously updated the work plans according to the Sat action." And then it says "report to us about all interesting occurrences and events, and about the realisation of the measures ordered according to the Sat action." Do you see that it says that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that. This Sat action was not a new one --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I'm just asking you if you can see that up on the screen, just so we don't get ahead of ourselves here. So we see -- you've told us that at this collegium meeting that you attended the SUP chief informed those present about the contents of this dispatch. And I take it that following that meeting, the different members or persons attending this meeting from the organisational units addressed in this dispatch would have proceeded to carry out the measures that are indicated in this dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, yes. Let me now tell you about Action Sat and other actions such as Action Valuta, Action Pariz, Action Suma. Those were typical actions undertaken by police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I'm just asking you a very precise question. We have very limited time, and I know you have a lot of information for the Court but unfortunately we can't explore it all in so much detail. So I don't want to interrupt you, but we just need to move on. So you said that they would implement the instructions, those attending the meetings and were concerned by these measures would implement them once they were briefed by the SUP chief, and this dispatch also instructs reporting on all interesting occurrences and about how the measures had been carried out in accordance with this Sat action. So I take it that was also something that was followed and implemented, that once these different members of organisational units addressed by this dispatch had carried out these measures, they would report on that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but we reported within our line of work. That is to say, to the administrations within the ministry seat. We would inform that. We didn't inform Mr. Djordjevic about these events because he was chief of the public security department. We would inform within our line of work. We would inform police administrations, and there were 11 of them, within the seat of the ministry. They were organisational units of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when you would inform the different police administrations and organisational units about the actions you had undertaken regarding action plan of the Sat action, you would refer to this dispatch, wouldn't you? You would indicate, we have carried out actions that are indicated as instructed in this dispatch number 1685? Isn't that how you would --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we would not normally refer to the dispatch. We would simply mention the action. We would say action Sat, and we would send it to the Secretariat of the Interior who would then forward it within separate lines of work to the MUP of Serbia and to the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you would not be, in fact, informing different police administrations, organisational units, as you said. You would send this information directly to the Djakovica SUP who would in turn send the information up the chain of command of the MUP; is that how it happened?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I was directly responsible to the chief of the secretariat. OUP, as an organisational unit, belongs to the Djakovica secretariat. So all of the reporting went via the secretariat and then the secretariat would forward it on to the staff, to the MUP, and to various administrations within their line of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So was the task of the secretariat in Djakovica to report on up to the MUP in Belgrade about the measures that had been taken to implement these instructions that were given in this dispatch, if I understand your evidence correctly?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but within their individual lines of work. MUP is a one whole, and it has various lines of work within it and various administrations dealing with various affairs, with police, with crime, with forensic work and so on. And it would also be sent to the staff, but not to Djordjevic directly. There was no such information channels leading directly to Djordjevic because those were minor matters that we did not inform Djordjevic of. We would inform our immediate superiors of these matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I understand what you are saying, that you would inform your immediate superiors of the actions you took. What I was asking whether in turn the SUP in Djakovica, and I'm speaking within the scope of work of the Djakovica SUP, would in turn inform the MUP in Belgrade about the measures that had been undertaken to implement this dispatch? Or would you not inform the public security department which was issuing this dispatch? By you I mean the SUP in Djakovica about the measures that had been taken to implement the dispatch?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would inform the staff, so the staff was the main body for Kosovo and Metohija and then the staff in turn would inform the minister, and if they found it necessary to send a circular letter, then they would send it to various chiefs within their line of work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what do you mean by circular letter, if they found it necessary to send a circular letter?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that kind of a letter is given to the duty service directly, which exists within the DOC operations centre within the MUP. And then they would compile a bulletin, bulletin within each separate line of work that would inform everybody else.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And when this bulletin was compiled, you are saying by the MUP staff, wouldn't they include also the public security department which had issued the dispatch in question instructing all SUP chiefs and other organisational units to undertake certain measures? Wouldn't it be logical to include the public security department in this -- such a communication?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but chiefs of crime police within various administrations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, I'm just speaking about the obligations that were given or the instructions given to SUP chiefs, we are not talking about crime police here. So I take it your answer is yes, that the public security department that specifically Mr. Djordjevic would receive a report up from the MUP staff saying that the measures -- these are the measures taken pursuant to the dispatch issued in September of 1998, dispatch number 1685?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if they found it necessary, if they found that there were indeed certain problems and that there were issues of major security importance, then, yes, but since this is done by crime operatives, then the chief of crime police administration or chief of police within the ministry seat would make the appropriate assessment concerning it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's move on from this dispatch. You indicated yesterday that you had members of the PJP attached to your OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I indicated that yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes. And you said yesterday that within your OUP there were usually at the level of one platoon, if I understood correctly, that's approximately 20 or 30 men, PJP members that were attached to your OUP?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And these PJP members belonged to -- or were attached to the Djakovica SUP, they were members of -- they belonged to the Djakovica SUP, is that what you said yesterday, if I recall correctly?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain this for you. When performing their regular duties and tasks, they belonged to the police station of the Decani OUP. When they were engaged as members of a PJP unit, then they would belong to the Djakovica SUP where a PJP company was established, so certain commanders would be also engaged within the Djakovica PJP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And do you know how large was the Djakovica PJP company?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A company normally has up to 100 members including the command staff, commanders of squads, commanders of platoons, and the company commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And if I understand correctly, this company from the Djakovica SUP would operate in Decani and also in Djakovica? They would carry out actions in both municipalities?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wherever the security situation so required, they carried out actions not only in Djakovica and in Decani, but in the broader area. PJP would come to Belgrade to ensure law and order there when the situation so required. But I had nothing to do with them when it comes to command responsibility. Nor did I take part in drafting plans for their work, plans for their activities. Nor did I know of their activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Very well, sir, we'll get to that in a minute. You said that the members of the Djakovica PJP company operated in other areas, not only in Decani and Djakovica. Did members of other PJP companies attached to other SUPs also come -- when it was required come to the Djakovica municipality and carried out actions there?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I was not informed about that, when it comes to those matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you know where members of your unit, your PJP unit carried out actions, but you do not know whether members of other PJP companies from other municipalities came to Djakovica -- Decani or whether they carried out any -- participated in any actions there?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't even know where my people were engaged, and logically I don't know where other people were engaged because they were under the command of the staff, under their direct command. Command of General Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. I see it's time for the break, Your Honours, and I also see my learned colleague is on his feet, but I hadn't seen him earlier, so I didn't stop my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the question has been answered, and it's time for our break, and I just had a minor observation because the question of my learned friend contains something that the witness had not spoken about, but in the meantime, the witness answered the question so that's all I have to say. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have the second break now and resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Kravetz.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we were just talking about PJP units, and I wanted to go back to that. I wanted to know if you could tell us how did the tasks that the PJP members of your OUP carry out compare with those -- you have no --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I think the witness has no interpretation. Are you getting interpretation now, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please repeat because at the outset I couldn't hear.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Yes, no problem, sir. I would like to go back to the issue we were discussing before the break, PJP units. And I was asking you how the task that PJP members from your OUP carry out compare with the ones that just regular policemen carried out. Were they different, were they the same, if you could tell us that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've already explained that during my testimony. A member of the PJP is a policeman who otherwise performs his regular police tasks. PJP engagement only takes place in extraordinary circumstances of natural disasters or other situations which demand particular attention, otherwise people who are regular policemen perform their usual tasks unless engaged in PJP units in such circumstances. These are no special police members.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. But let me rephrase my question then. Let's talk about 1998, the task carried out by members of PJP units from your OUP, were they the same as regular police officers or were they different when they were engaged as part of a PJP unit, I mean?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were regular policemen engaged in certain conditions to take part in PJP activities.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And what were those?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, disturbances of law and order in the area. Natural disasters and similar situations. For example, situations in which the integrity of the Republic of Serbia comes into question. It's circumstances such as those.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in 1998, we are speaking specifically about Kosovo, what sort of activities were PJP units carrying out? Members of PJP in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. You would need to ask the staff about that, and the commanders of companies and battalions. So first of all, you would need to speak to General Lukic, commander of the staff who decided upon it. I didn't busy myself with that, and it was not within my purview.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday when you were asked about how PJP and members of PJPs were assembled and deployed on the basis of whose order, this is at transcript page 67, you said, I would always be informed of their engagement and deployment of the members of the PJP, Decani OUP who were within the composition of the Djakovica SUP. Do you remember saying that? I'm referring to line 12 of -- I don't have --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes. Being informed was a different thing and knowing what part of what unit they made, but I wasn't privy to their tasks, so we have to distinguish between the two different situations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague is on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. I can watch that, thank you. Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the question that was put given that it was without a reference -- well, the witness never mentioned any deployments. He did mention members being sent to certain tasks, but nothing of this sort was uttered by the witness. If I'm mistaken I stand to be corrected, and I would kindly ask for a reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the reference is at transcript page 67 of yesterday's transcript. Unfortunately the version of yesterday's transcript that I have in e-court does not have updated transcript pages, and this is lines 12 to 14 of page 67 that I'm referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And the witness referred to deployment twice in that passage.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, sir, you also said, and this is the following page, transcript page 68, that when the unit returned after completing their tasks, the chief of the police substation would inform about this and you would receive a copy. Do you remember saying that yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Informing, it means that that part of the unit, platoon, returned from the field and were supposed to go back to their regular duties. This was nothing out of ordinary. If they were sent to address the services of law and order, they would be dispatched to perform their task and then go back to their police station in Decani where they were answerable to the police station commander.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, you've told us several times now that you had no knowledge of the activities or the tasks, specific tasks that the PJP units of your OUP were engaged with. I take it, sir, that you were aware of the fact that they were engaged in actions against the KLA, that much you knew?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All those PJP units certainly took part in actions against the KLA. This is no secret.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: You've told --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I didn't know in what area they were engaged or on the basis of what plan, and who sent them there. This was not a part of my work to now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us today that you've always had detailed information from intelligence sources about the KLA. Do you remember saying that? This is at page 8 of today's transcript.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, I can say so. I had lots of information. I could spend a week here talking to you about the way the KLA was created and carried out its activities. I used to work for the state security service, remember, and I could go on and on about this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So, sir, you are saying that you had detailed information about what the KLA was doing in your municipality, but you did not know what members of your OUP that were attached to a PJP unit, you did not know what sort of actions they were carrying out?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, one can suppose they had clashes with the terrorists, but as to where they were sent, to what locations and following what plans, this was not -- that was something up to me to know. A commander didn't need to know that. They were immediately transferred under the authority of the PJP, they received their new commander and units and new line of subordination. They were subordinated directly to General Lukic and the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, just so we are clear, I'm not suggesting that you were the commander of a PJP unit. I'm just trying to clarify your knowledge about their activities, so I am not suggesting that you commanded them. What I don't understand, sir, is how you could have so much detailed information about activities of the KLA and clashes that occurred but not know where the PJP members of your OUP were carrying out activities. That doesn't make much sense, does it, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it does because my OUP members who were transferred under the authority of the PJP were not supposed to inform me. They were supposed to inform the staff, and they were completely under the staff's authority. They were supposed to inform the staff about every event which took place. The staff was the body in charge of command and control of PJP members. As for the PJP, I had -- I also had contacts in the KLA, so ten years later, I can tell you how they were created, who recruited them, how they were trained, what finances they received and everything else. I can tell you about their logistical support. Anything that you might want to know. I could go on for a week addressing only the creation of the KLA and their finance sources, training methods, how money and weapons were transferred, I can explain that in detail, including all the crimes they committed in Decani municipality.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, you did not receive any information from the Djakovica SUP chief about where members of PJP units would be engaged in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't need to inform me about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are saying you knew what the KLA was doing but you knew nothing else that was going on in your municipality, where there were confrontations with the police, where the police was carrying out activities? You did not know that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this again brings us back to certain questions. You are trying to tell me to tell you something which was not part of my work. All plans and engagement of forces ... I don't know where my men were, whether in this or that municipality, but this was not how it worked in practice and the minister did not get into that. He only issued instructions on the establishment and functioning as well as command within the PJP. I've already tried to address that, and as for the KLA, I can go on for a week and corroborate that with all evidence you might need, but this a is different procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: The drawing up of plans for the prevention of terrorism, wasn't that within the scope or the purview of the work of SUPs?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plans were sent directly to the staff. To repeat what I said already, two sectors, the public security and state security sector established the staff by decision of the minister in Pristina. It had clear command structure, decision-making structure, they knew exactly who drew up plans and issued orders, and you have probably been able to see that yourself in the documents you have.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: When you say plans were sent directly to the staff, by whom were they sent to the staff?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that plans were sent directly to the staff but were created by the staff, in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And in order to create plans for the actions that were going to be carried out within the different municipalities, didn't the staff require the input of the SUPs, specifically of SUP chiefs?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It didn't necessarily have to be like that. I've already told you that David Gajic from the security service was deputy head of the staff, and they engaged in operative work. Based on such information and based on their assessments, they drew up plans which I didn't see. I'm not familiar with those. Therefore, I can't tell you of anything that I wasn't privy to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are saying that the plans that were drawn up by the MUP staff were based on information that only came from the security service? Wasn't there also an input from the SUPs?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there probably were other sources from other services. It's not only the state security. You probably know that there was public security service and others, but most of it was in terms of collecting data by intelligence work, and this fell within the scope of the services I referred to. It is the state security sector who engaged in that primarily.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you are not aware of SUPs being requested or required to draw up any plans for combatting terrorism in the respective municipalities by the MUP staff? You are not aware of that happening?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. No one asked me to do anything of the sort within my OUP.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Well, let me show you a document, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could have P689 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And these, sir, are the minutes of a meeting at the MUP staff in Pristina held on the 2nd of December, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we could go to the next page, page 3, I believe, on both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So we see there the list of those present, and it includes all chiefs of SUPs and the commanders of the detachments, and we see General Lukic there along with other officers; do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. There were others meaning members of PJP detachments, commanders of those. This is what you omitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That's what I just said. Chiefs of SUPs, and just to correct the transcript at line 10, it's SUP and commanders of detachments.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 4, and it's the middle of the page in the B/C/S and in the English it's the bottom of page 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So we see here on this page, sir, that the different SUP chiefs are reporting on their activities. If we could scroll down in the English. And we see on your screen in the B/C/S it's somewhere toward the lower half of the page, we see that the Djakovica SUP chief who is identified here as deputy chief Kovacevic is reporting about activities, and he reports not only about the situation in sector -- well, he reports about the situation in the sector of the Djakovica SUP and also about terrorist attacks and provocations specifically in the areas of Glodjani and Decani. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we could go to page 5, bottom in the B/C/S and page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I comment on this, on this meeting?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: In a minute I'll let you comment, sir. If we could just move on to page 5 bottom in the B/C/S simply to show you, and it's page 6 in the English, that at the conclusion of this report, we see Major-General Sreten Lukic giving -- he speaks, and he gives a number of instructions which continue on the next page. Do you see that, sir, that's at the bottom of your page in the B/C/S, General Lukic speaks? Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Right in the bottom.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It Blagoje Pesic or further up the page?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Right below Blagoje Pesic.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major-General Sreten Lukic, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we continue to page 7 in the B/C/S and page 8 in the English, this is the continuation of General Lukic's instructions. He provides -- he issues a series of tasks at the conclusion of this meeting. You see that? And what I'm looking for is on the next page. Page 8 in the -- yes. And at the conclusion of this meeting we see that General Lukic says: "By 7 December 1998 you need to submit a plan for the prevention of terrorism, which in principle should contain:" And there are eight points of the information that needs to be included in that plan. You see that, sir, that --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: General Lukic is tasking those present with the preparation of a plan for the prevention of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, I want to move on to a related document, and this is P1043. And this is a meeting of the MUP staff which takes place some weeks later on 21st, December, 1998. And it will come up on your screen shortly. We see on the first page the list of attendees. This one includes MUP minister Stojiljkovic and also General Obrad Stevanovic, General Lukic, and we see at the bottom that all chiefs of SUP and also commanders of PJP detachments are there. Do you see that, sir? I believe we have that also on the B/C/S, on the screen.

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we can go to page 3 in the B/C/S and page 5 in the English. And it's the bottom of the page in both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And here we have the Djakovica SUP chief Kovacevic again reporting on the activities in his SUP area, and he says: "The police undertook an operation to sweep the terrain in the Glodjani village sector and drove away some 50 to 60 terrorists from it and killed two." Then he says: "We adopted a plan to combat terrorism, and it is mostly being carried out."

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, do you want me to comment?

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: This is Glodjani village, where is that located?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 10 kilometres from Decani itself in the territory of that municipality. As for what Mr. Kovacevic said, he was in the wider composition, the wider circle of the staff. His report is based on the information he had received from the field as a SUP chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And who would he have received that information from in the field?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he probably received field information from PJP members.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, we saw -- we see in that passage that he is referring to the plan to combat terrorism, and he says, we have adopted it and it's mostly being carried out. This is the same plan that General Lukic had instructed those present at the 2nd December meeting to prepare; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not to prepare. They drew up a plan and implemented it, as far as I can see based on the document. Of course, I'm not familiar with it, but my interpretation is similar to yours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So this is the same plan that General Lukic instructed SUP chiefs to draw up and implement at the other MUP staff meeting that we saw on 2nd December; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand you. What do you mean the same plan? Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, we had just looked at the MUP staff minutes -- I mean, the minutes of a MUP staff meeting of 2nd December where General Lukic instructed those present to draw up a plan to combat terrorism by the 7th of December. Remember we just saw that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: What I'm putting to you, sir, here is that the SUP chief of the Djakovica SUP is saying that he is implementing that that plan, in fact, has been drawn up and that it's being mostly carried out. That's what he is saying; correct?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot claim that. I do not control the work of the chief of the Djakovica SUP, nor did I take part in drafting the plans. There were certain things that were done confidentially, under confidential circumstances. So I cannot tell you something I don't know. So the relationship between the chief of the secretariat and the staff is something that I'm not privy to. It was strictly confidential. And it was up to them to decide how to draw up plans, who would be doing it, at which level. I knew nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So earlier, sir, when I asked you whether these plans to combat terrorism were drafted with the MUP staff with input from SUPs, you essentially said no, that the MUP staff acted with information from state security; that's what you said, no?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not exactly as you put it. As I have told you, all plans were drawn up at the staff. All assessments were made there and then orders were issued for tasks to be carried out. You probably misunderstood me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, what I'm asking you is whether that was done with input from SUPs, and earlier you had told me no, and now you are telling me that the relationship between the chief of the SUP and the staff was strictly confidential so you wouldn't know if they were drawing up plans; is that what you are saying now?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've said what I've said, and it also depended on the situation. The situation changed from one minute to the next. Sometimes there were unwritten rules, so it's not like the rule was written down in stone. That's how it always had to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: If we can move on in the same document, page 6 in the B/C/S and page 9 in the English. And just for clarity, the passage we are going to look at is -- it refers to something stated by General Stevanovic, which in the English begins on the previous page. I believe in the B/C/S it's all on one page. So if we could go to the bottom of page 9, and in the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And it says there, this is General Stevanovic speaking: "You made plans to combat terrorism and submitted them to the staff. It is the assessment of the staff that they are mostly being implemented." Do you see that passage, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Now, if we go to the next page in the English, and we are still on page 6, fifth bullet point in the B/C/S, this is still General Stevanovic speaking, he says -- I'm sorry, I'm losing my voice: "Broader actions towards terrorist basis should be plans by the ministry staff; however, the initiative should be with the secretariats who should make preparations and compile recommendations of the activity plan. All plans should be based on the principles of police operation." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can see it very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So isn't General Stevanovic saying here that although the plans for anti-terrorist actions are planned by the MUP staff, the initiative to do these is with the SUPs who are, in fact, better placed to know what the situation is in their area of responsibility, no?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my view, this is more about some pieces of information, some intelligence rather than plans. It says here, Plans, but those were really some security assessments that the secretariats could send to the staff so that they could draw up a plan on the basis of that. That wasn't a general plan.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Okay. So just going back to my initial question, and following up from your answer, in order for the MUP of staff to draw up plans, it needed the input from SUPs who had the information of what was going on on the ground; correct? You are saying they would provide security assessments, that was information required to know where to carry out police actions, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you put it yourself, I have nothing to add. It's as you put it. But you keep forgetting that there is also the public -- rather the state security department which was within the staff, and that's not something you should neglect because the state security is the intelligence service, and that's something that you should never, never neglect when talking about these things.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, all I'm trying to clarify is just the role of SUPs in the drawing up of these plans, that is all I am trying to clarify here. And it was you who said that the secretariats, you said it says here, Plans, but those were really some security assessments that the secretariats could send to the staff. So you are saying that the secretariats sent information to the staff from what I understand it, so that they could draw up a plan on the basis of that? Isn't that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wasn't informed of that. I wasn't aware of that, but it would be logical for them to make a sort of an assessment in that situation. Let me reiterate, the state security service was the one who provided intelligence and who took part in drafting the plans because the deputy --

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: We are not talking about the state security service, sir. I'm just bringing you back to my question which had to do with the role of SUPs. And I'm understanding that you are agreeing with me that the MUP staff required information. I'm not saying that was the only source, just so we are clear, I am not saying that was the exclusive source was information provided by the SUPs, but they did require chiefs of SUPs to provide information in order to be able to draw plans for police actions?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that. I don't know about that. I suppose that there may have been such cases in some situations.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see Mr. Popovic is sort of on his feet, sitting back down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, once again, the witness has answered the question, but for the third time the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Mr. Popovic. I keep having to repeat it. It's borne out of the experience of the interventions that happened earlier in this trial. Where a witness is not being in any way overborne, as this witness clearly is not, the witness is being allowed to answer questions. If there is then an objection that is well-founded, we will take it into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. So you said that you were not aware that plans drawn up by the MUP staff had any input from SUPs. Are you saying, sir, that if police actions were going to be carried out in your municipality, you also did not provide any input or were requested to provide any input to the Djakovica SUP as to where there were problem areas or issues that needed to be addressed regarding the KLA in your municipality? You were never asked to do that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because they knew what was happening on the ground. They had intelligence available to them. There were members of state security in every secretariat, and they made their own assessments. That was something that was well known to everybody in the Djakovica SUP even within the office of the police department. So the entire area was covered by terrorists and terrorist groups, and one didn't need to have great knowledge and great expertise to study that in detail.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: And your evidence, sir, is that you knew nothing about any sort of police actions carried out in your municipality? Actions carried out by PJP units, you knew nothing about that?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have told you, I heard that actions were being carried out, but I wasn't directly involved in them. I wasn't involved in drafting any plans. It was a well known fact that there were terrorist activities in the entire territory of Kosovo and Metohija. That area was inundated by terrorists and terrorist activities of a large scale.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: That is exactly why I'm asking the question, sir. I mean, you were in a municipality where there was extensive action -- or there were extensive actions carried out by the police against the KLA, and earlier you told us that you knew nothing of the activities of the PJP units and you had nothing to do with them. And now you are saying that you heard that actions were being carried out?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I had nothing to do when it comes to command responsibility. I wasn't involved in drafting the plans. I didn't know about their scope of work and the area where they carried out that work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Sir, I will tell you again just to clarify, I'm not suggesting anything dealing with command responsibility. I'm just trying to understand your scope of knowledge of the police actions being carried out on the ground. And earlier you told us that you knew nothing about the activities of police units, and now you are telling us that you heard that actions were carried out?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait a minute, I can't understand anything that I heard. Well, one could interpret it in many ways. One could hear gun-fire in the vicinity, fire from heavy artillery, heavy guns. One could hear that actions were carried out.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: So you were aware that actions were being carried out by PJP units in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: VUKMIR MIRCIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did hear, but I didn't know that they were supposed to be carried out and when.

utterances.speaker: MS. KRAVETZ
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we've reached the end of the session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we must adjourn now. We will resume tomorrow morning at 9.00. We must adjourn now. A Court Officer will assist you when we adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 24th day of March, 2010, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
